background.task:
**Task completed successfully.** The MockSite Electronics category page (`http://localhost:18080/ec/b?node=1292115012`) was navigated, snapshotted, inspected, and fully extracted with a single X-SQL query covering every required DOM/STR/ARRAY function, PowerCSS `:expr()`, and WHERE/ORDER BY/LIMIT. All extracted values were verified against the raw page markup (exported to `page-ec-listing.html` in this run's scratch dir).

### Final query (`.test-sessions/20261013T0154334271610Z/query-final.sql`)

```sql
SELECT
    STR_ABBREVIATE(STR_TRIM(ARRAY_FIRST_NOT_BLANK(MAKE_ARRAY(
        DOM_FIRST_TEXT(DOM, '.product-title'),
        DOM_FIRST_ATTR(DOM, 'img.product-img', 'alt'),
        DOM_FIRST_TEXT(DOM, 'a.product-link'),
        'Untitled product'
    ))), 22) AS title,
    DOM_FIRST_FLOAT(DOM, '.product-price', 0.0) AS price,
    STR_FIRST_FLOAT(ARRAY_FIRST_NOT_BLANK(MAKE_ARRAY(
        DOM_FIRST_ATTR(DOM, '.product-rating', 'data-rating'),
        DOM_FIRST_TEXT(DOM, '.product-rating')
    )), 0.0) AS rating,
    DOM_FIRST_HREF(DOM, 'a.product-link') AS link,
    DOM_FIRST_IMG(DOM, 'img.product-img') AS image,
    STR_DEFAULT_IF_BLANK(DOM_FIRST_ATTR(DOM, '.product-card', 'data-category-id'), 'uncategorized') AS category_id,
    STR_UPPER_CASE(ARRAY_FIRST_NOT_BLANK(MAKE_ARRAY(
        DOM_FIRST_TEXT(DOM, '.product-badges'),
        'standard'
    ))) AS badge
FROM DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, 'div.product-card:expr(width > 180 && height > 250)')
WHERE CAST(DOM_FIRST_FLOAT(DOM, '.product-price', 0.0) AS DOUBLE) >= 25.0
  AND STR_FIRST_FLOAT(DOM_FIRST_TEXT(DOM, '.product-rating'), 0.0) >= 4.2
ORDER BY CAST(DOM_FIRST_FLOAT(DOM, '.product-price', 0.0) AS DOUBLE) DESC
LIMIT 5
```

issues.title: inspect's "Try these next" image/link suggestions omit `all` — silently return only the first URL

sections.body:
1) ./b4w.ps1 -s xsql-eval htmlsnapshot inspect --max 3 --depth 3
2) Copy and run the suggested line: ./b4w.ps1 -s xsql-eval htmlsnapshot get attr "img[src]" src --limit 20  # image URLs
3) Compare with the correct form: ./b4w.ps1 -s xsql-eval htmlsnapshot get all attr "img[src]" src --limit 20
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The suggestion labeled '# image URLs' / '# link URLs' should list ALL matching image/link URLs (as the sibling `get all text …` suggestions do), i.e. it should invoke `htmlsnapshot get all attr`.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The suggested command exits 0 and prints exactly ONE URL (the first match, an unrelated placeholder image); `--limit 20` is silently ignored, so a user copying the tool's own suggestion for batch extraction gets silently partial data with no error or warning.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The suggestion strings are hard-coded and inconsistent: the `get all text` lines pass the correct subcommand, but the image/link-url lines were written as `htmlsnapshot get attr …` (missing `all`). The stray `--limit 20` on single `get` is additionally tolerated by the parser (see related unknown-flag issue), so the mistake fails silently instead of erroring. Same strings duplicated in three places (inspect renderer + capture tip).
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_html_snapshot_inspect() lines ~11332-11347 (also ~11345-11347 fallback branch) and handle_html_snapshot_capture() lines ~9203-9206
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Change the emitted lines to `htmlsnapshot get all attr "img[src]" src --limit 20`, `htmlsnapshot get all attr "a[href]" href --limit 20`, and the `:expr` large-images variant to use `get all`
- Generate these suggestion lines from one shared helper so the three call sites cannot drift apart again
- Add a unit/integration test asserting every printed 'Try these next' command parses as a valid command (e.g. rejects `get` combined with `--limit`)
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Unrecognized/misplaced flags are silently ignored by htmlsnapshot get / get all (e.g. --bogus)

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s xsql-eval htmlsnapshot get text "div.product-title" --bogus 1   → prints '4K OLED TV 55', exit 0
./b4w.ps1 -s xsql-eval htmlsnapshot get all text "div.product-title" --bogus 1   → prints all 6 titles, exit 0
./b4w.ps1 -s xsql-eval htmlsnapshot get text "div.product-title" --limit 20   → prints 1 title, exit 0 (flag ignored)
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: An unknown flag should be a usage error (the CLI already rejects other stray flags, e.g. `-s` placed after the command, with the hint 'global flags must appear before the command'), or at minimum produce a stderr warning naming the ignored flag.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Unknown `--flag value` pairs are accepted silently; the command runs with default semantics and exit 0. A typo'd flag (e.g. `--abslute`, `--lmmit`) silently changes behavior with no feedback.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: parse_raw_args() inserts every `--key value` token into a params map without validating it against the invoked command's declared option set; per-command tool_params builders read only known keys, so unknown keys disappear without a trace.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/args.rs:parse_raw_args() (line 223) — validation would need the command's declared option set, available near the dispatch layer in cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Validate parsed flag keys against the command's declared options and reject unrecognized ones with the existing usage-error style
- If lenient parsing is deliberate (e.g. MCP passthrough), emit a stderr warning listing ignored flags
- Add a regression test that `htmlsnapshot get text "h1" --bogus 1` fails (or warns) instead of succeeding silently
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: X-SQL reference says 'no joins' but a JOIN of two DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT sources executes successfully

sections.body:
Write probe-join.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, 'div.product-card') a JOIN DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, 'div.product-card') b ON 1=1
Run: ./b4w.ps1 -s xsql-eval htmlsnapshot query --sql "@…/probe-join.sql" --format table
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Per skills/browser4-cli/references/x-sql.md ('No other SQL syntax is supported — no CTEs (WITH), no subqueries in FROM, no EXPLODE, no joins'), the query should be rejected.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Executes successfully: 1 row, n = 36 (= 6 cards × 6 cards). (For contrast, CTEs are indeed rejected, and COUNT(*) aggregates work — both as documented.) The CLI's own hint text 'The SQL variant lets you query with full expressive power (joins, filters, aggregates)' is therefore right about joins while the reference says they are impossible.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The restriction documented in x-sql.md is at least partly policy-only: SQLTemplate.createSQL() produces a plain SELECT that H2 executes, and no backend validation rejects JOINed table-function sources. Either enforcement is missing or the doc is stale; the two sources of truth need reconciling. Note joins duplicate page loads per source, which may be why they are discouraged.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: skills/browser4-cli/references/x-sql.md (constraint block above 'URL parameter', line ~23); enforcement would live in the backend X-SQL validation layer (browser4-rest scrape session / SQLTemplate)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Decide the real contract, then make docs and behavior agree: either state which JOIN forms are supported (and their page-load cost) or reject JOIN at validation time with a 4xx
- Mention that aggregates (COUNT/SUM) and self-joins behave differently from the blanket 'no joins' statement
- Add a test pinning the accepted FROM-clause grammar so docs cannot drift again
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Rejected non-SELECT X-SQL (CTE) returns HTTP 500 instead of the documented 400/417

sections.body:
Write probe-cte.sql:
WITH cards AS (SELECT DOM_FIRST_TEXT(DOM, '.product-title') AS t FROM DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, 'div.product-card'))
SELECT t FROM cards LIMIT 3
Run: ./b4w.ps1 -s xsql-eval htmlsnapshot query --sql "@…/probe-cte.sql" --format table
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: According to skills/browser4-cli/references/htmlsnapshot.md's status table, an X-SQL syntax/query error should surface as 400 Bad Request (or 417 Expectation Failed), letting callers distinguish bad input from backend failure.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error' with message 'Only select statements are supported'; the CLI prints '### X-SQL Query Failed (500 Internal Server Error) — Check the backend logs for details' and exits 1. A user input rejection is reported as a server fault.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The backend's pre-validation ('Only select statements are supported') maps to statusCode 500 in the response envelope instead of a 4xx client-error class. The CLI faithfully forwards the server status.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Map the non-SELECT rejection to 400 Bad Request in the backend query endpoint (a client-usable error), or 417 to match the existing convention for query failures
- If 500 is intentional for this class, update the htmlsnapshot.md status table so scripts branch correctly
- Make the CLI hint distinguish 'your query was rejected' from 'the backend broke'
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

Then check ./b4w.ps1 --help htmlsnapshot — no mention of `w=`.

sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:9103 (extras.push(format!("w={}", weight))) — help text in cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Document the weight in `--help htmlsnapshot` (e.g. 'w = visual-prominence weight; elements are sorted by it, descending')
- Consider labeling it `weight=` in the output so it is self-describing

issues.title: Numeric X-SQL results serialize as JSON strings in --result-only output

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s xsql-eval htmlsnapshot query --sql "@…/query-final.sql" --result-only  → {"title": "4K OLED TV 55", "price": "899.99", "rating": "4.6", …}
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Machine-readable output should either carry JSON numbers for numeric-returning functions (DOM_FIRST_FLOAT, STR_FIRST_FLOAT) or document that they are emitted as strings.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: price and rating are quoted strings ('899.99', '4.6'); consumers must parse them. (Workaround: wrap the expression in a numeric cast in the SELECT list, e.g. CAST(DOM_FIRST_FLOAT(…) AS DOUBLE).)
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: DOM_FIRST_FLOAT/STR_FIRST_FLOAT values ride custom H2 value types whose serialization is string-based; the JSON envelope copies that string form.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add a line to skills/browser4-cli/references/x-sql.md: numeric-returning functions serialize as strings unless CAST(… AS DOUBLE) is selected
- Consider emitting JSON numbers for ValueFloat/ValueInt in the resultSet encoder so the default output is type-correct
- Show the typed example in the x-sql.md quick-reference so users write machine-friendly queries by default
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
